channel.title: Hominin History
channel.description: Articles on human evolution: hominin species, fossil sites, ancient DNA and the Stone Age.

item.title: Yamnaya: The Steppe Herders Who Remade Europe’s DNA
item.description: The Yamnaya were steppe herders whose ancestry runs through most Europeans. What 216 ancient genomes in our atlas show, and why the language link is debated.

item.title: Cheddar Man: What His DNA Really Says About His Skin
item.description: Cheddar Man, Britain’s oldest near-complete skeleton, got dark skin in 2018. What his 10,000-year-old genome reveals, and where that skin call falls short.

item.title: Early European Farmers: The Anatolian DNA Trail
item.description: Early European farmers descended from Neolithic Anatolians who carried farming west 8,000 years ago. How four DNA studies and 110 atlas genomes trace the route.

item.title: Mal’ta Boy: The Ice Age Child Linking Europe and America
item.description: The Mal’ta boy lived near Lake Baikal 24,000 years ago, yet his genome links Europeans and Native Americans. How one child’s arm bone redrew the Ice Age map.

item.title: Ust’-Ishim Man: The 45,000-Year-Old Genome From Siberia
item.description: A thigh bone from a Siberian riverbank yielded a 45,000-year-old genome read 42 times over. How Ust’-Ishim man’s Neanderthal DNA works as a clock for our past.

item.title: Toumaï Skull: The 7-Million-Year-Old Bipedalism Fight
item.description: The Toumaï skull from Chad may be the oldest known hominin. Why a forgotten thigh bone and six rival studies now decide if Sahelanthropus walked upright.

item.title: Laetoli Footprints: 3.66-Million-Year-Old Walkers
item.description: The Laetoli footprints froze a 3.66-million-year-old walk in volcanic ash. Who made the tracks, how tall they stood, and the new trails that rewrote the story.

item.title: Australopithecus sediba: Ancestor of Homo or Side Branch?
item.description: Australopithecus sediba pairs a Homo-like hand and pelvis with a 420 cc brain. What the Malapa skeletons show, and why its claim to be our ancestor is in doubt.

item.title: Dmanisi Hominins: Five Skulls That Left Africa Early
item.description: The Dmanisi hominins reached Georgia 1.8 million years ago with brains as small as 546 cc. What Skull 5 and a toothless elder reveal about the first Eurasians.

item.title: Shanidar Neanderthals: Care, Burial and the Flower Myth
item.description: The Shanidar Neanderthals of Iraqi Kurdistan include a disabled man who survived for years and a woman buried 75,000 years ago. Was the flower burial real?

item.title: The Schöningen Spears: Oldest Complete Wooden Weapons
item.description: Found in a German coal mine, the Schöningen spears are the oldest complete hunting weapons. How they were made, who used them, and why they ended a big debate.

item.title: Do Chimpanzees Have a Stone Age? Primate Archaeology
item.description: Chimpanzees left stone tools 4,300 years ago, and monkeys have used hammers for 3,000. How primate archaeology compares with the first human tools.

item.title: Why Is Human Childbirth So Hard? The Obstetric Dilemma
item.description: Human childbirth is unusually difficult and often needs help. The obstetric dilemma, the rival energetics theory, and what fossil pelvises reveal about the origin.

item.title: Is Human Evolution Still Happening? The Evidence
item.description: Humans are still evolving. Sea nomads with bigger spleens, Tibetan altitude genes, sickle-cell trait and the claims that turned out to be wrong, explained.

item.title: Kennewick Man (The Ancient One): DNA, Dispute, Reburial
item.description: Found in 1996, Kennewick Man is a 9,000-year-old skeleton that sparked a 20-year fight between scientists and tribes. What his DNA showed, and how it ended.

item.title: Ötzi the Iceman: What a 5,300-Year-Old Body Reveals
item.description: Ötzi the Iceman died in the Alps 5,300 years ago with an arrow in his shoulder. His genome, tattoos, last meal and copper axe reveal a life in the Copper Age.

item.title: How Long Did Early Humans Live? Stone Age Life Expectancy
item.description: Did Stone Age people die at 30? Not quite. How long early humans, Neanderthals and hunter-gatherers really lived, and why average life expectancy is so misleading.

item.title: The Oldest Musical Instruments: Ice Age Flutes and More
item.description: The oldest musical instruments are 40,000-year-old flutes of bird bone and ivory. Plus a disputed Neanderthal flute and an Ice Age conch that still plays.

item.title: When Were Dogs Domesticated? The Ice Age Origins of Dogs
item.description: Dogs were the first domestic animal, tamed by Ice Age hunters from a wolf population that no longer exists. What ancient DNA reveals about when and where.

item.title: When Did Humans Start Wearing Clothes? The Evidence
item.description: Clothing rarely fossilises, so how do we know when humans started wearing it? Lice DNA, bone tools, skinned foxes and 30,000-year-old flax fibres tell the story.

item.title: Why Do Humans Have Different Skin Colors? The Evolution
item.description: Human skin colour tracks UV light, balancing folate against vitamin D. How dark skin evolved, why light skin evolved more than once, and what ancient DNA adds.

item.title: Why Can Some Adults Drink Milk? Lactose Tolerance Evolution
item.description: Most adults can't digest milk. The mutation that lets some of us do it spread astonishingly fast, and ancient DNA shows it happened later than anyone thought.

item.title: Did Humans Nearly Go Extinct? Toba and the Bottleneck
item.description: Did a supervolcano cut humans to a few thousand survivors? The Toba hypothesis, the 900,000-year-old bottleneck claim, and what the evidence really shows.

item.title: The Taung Child: The Fossil That Put Africa First
item.description: In 1924 a box of quarry rubble reached Raymond Dart. Inside was the Taung Child, the first Australopithecus. Why experts rejected it, and how an eagle killed it.

item.title: The Piltdown Man Hoax: How a Fake Fossil Fooled Science
item.description: Piltdown Man was a medieval human skull and an orangutan jaw, stained and filed to look ancient. How the hoax fooled science for 40 years, and who did it.

item.title: Did Neanderthals Bury Their Dead? What the Evidence Shows
item.description: From La Chapelle-aux-Saints to the Shanidar flower burial, the evidence that Neanderthals buried their dead — and the arguments against it.

item.title: How Ancient DNA Works: Reading Genomes From Fossils
item.description: How do scientists get DNA from a 400,000-year-old bone? Damage patterns, petrous bones, clean rooms and cave dirt — the science of ancient DNA explained.

item.title: Why Are Human Brains So Big? The Leading Theories
item.description: Our brains tripled in size in two million years and burn a fifth of our energy. Cooking, social groups and cheaper guts — the theories, weighed.

item.title: When Did Humans Reach Australia? 65,000 Years of Evidence
item.description: Humans reached Australia at least 50,000 and possibly 65,000 years ago, crossing open sea to Sahul. The archaeology, the genetics and the debate.

item.title: When Did Humans Reach the Americas? The Evidence
item.description: Footprints at White Sands push human arrival in the Americas back to 23,000 years ago. How the Clovis-first model collapsed, and what replaced it.

item.title: How Many Human Species Were There? The Full List
item.description: At least 21 hominin species have been named, and several coexisted. Here is the full list, when each lived, and why being the only one left is unusual.

item.title: Dragon Man (Homo longi): The Skull That Was a Denisovan
item.description: Hidden in a Chinese well for 85 years, the Harbin cranium was named Homo longi in 2021. In 2025, DNA from its dental calculus identified it as Denisovan.

item.title: Homo luzonensis: The Small Hominin of the Philippines
item.description: Homo luzonensis, named in 2019 from Callao Cave on Luzon, mixes modern teeth with australopith-like curved toes. Who were they, and how did they get there?

item.title: Who Was Homo erectus? The First Truly Global Human
item.description: Homo erectus survived nearly two million years and spread from Africa to Java. Meet the longest-lived human species and what made it so successful.

item.title: Lucy the Australopithecus: The Fossil That Changed Everything
item.description: Lucy, the 3.2-million-year-old Australopithecus afarensis skeleton from Ethiopia, proved we walked upright before our brains grew. Her full story.

item.title: The First Cannibals: Cannibalism Across Human Evolution
item.description: Cannibalism in human evolution: from Homo antecessor at Gran Dolina 800,000 years ago to Neanderthals and Ice Age humans. What the butchered bones reveal.

item.title: Did Neanderthals Have Red Hair? Their Skin, Hair and Eye Colour
item.description: Did Neanderthals have red hair? Ancient DNA reveals their likely skin, hair and eye colour, and why some carried a pale, red-haired variant unlike our own.

item.title: Why Do Humans Have Chins? The Only Primate With One
item.description: Why do humans have chins? We are the only species with a bony chin, not even Neanderthals had one. Explore the leading theories for this strange feature.

item.title: How Did Humans Lose Their Body Hair?
item.description: Why did humans lose their body hair? Explore the sweat-and-endurance theory, and how the DNA of lice reveals when our ancestors became the 'naked ape'.

item.title: The World's Oldest Cave Art: Who Made It, and Where?
item.description: The world's oldest cave art includes a 45,500-year-old pig in Indonesia and Spanish marks over 64,000 years old. Who were the first artists?

item.title: What Did Neanderthals Hunt? Predators and Prey of Ice Age Europe
item.description: Neanderthals hunted reindeer, horse, bison and even mammoth and 13-tonne straight-tusked elephants, while sharing the cold with cave lions, hyenas and bears.

item.title: Animals Homo erectus Encountered: Life Among the Giants
item.description: From Dmanisi to Java, Homo erectus shared the land with giant hyenas, sabre-toothed cats, the huge ape Gigantopithecus and elephants of every size.

item.title: Hunted, Not Hunters: The Predators That Stalked Australopithecus
item.description: Small upright australopiths were prey, not hunters. Eagles, leopards, giant hyenas and false sabre-tooths stalked them, and killed the famous Taung Child.

item.title: The Strange Animals of Flores: Homo floresiensis and Its Island World
item.description: The metre-tall hobbit shared Flores with dwarf elephants, giant rats, Komodo dragons and a stork nearly two metres tall. Meet its lost island world.

item.title: Cave Bears and Humans: A 400,000-Year Relationship
item.description: The giant cave bear shared Europe's caves with Neanderthals for 400,000 years, inspiring Ice Age art and the debunked myth of a 'cave bear cult'.

item.title: The Dwarf Elephants of Ice Age Sicily — and the Cyclops Myth
item.description: Ice Age Sicily and Malta had elephants the size of ponies. Their one-holed skulls may be the fossils behind the ancient Greek myth of the Cyclops.

item.title: Could Other Human Species Talk? The Evidence for Ancient Language
item.description: Language doesn't fossilise, but hyoid bones, ear anatomy, the FOXP2 gene and symbolic behaviour all hint that Neanderthals could speak. Here is the evidence.

item.title: Ice Age Animals Early Humans Encountered: From Homo erectus to the First Americans
item.description: Ice age animals early humans encountered — from the mammoths and cave lions Neanderthals and Denisovans knew to the American lion the first Americans faced.

item.title: How Do We Know What Extinct Humans Ate?
item.description: Food rots, but diet leaves fingerprints. See how isotopes, tooth wear, dental tartar and cut marks reveal what extinct humans really ate.

item.title: What Makes Us Human? The Traits That Set Us Apart
item.description: What makes us human? Explore the biological and behavioural traits — bipedalism, big brains, tools, language and cumulative culture — and when each one evolved.

item.title: The Out of Africa Theory Explained
item.description: The Out of Africa theory explained: how and when Homo sapiens arose in Africa ~300,000 years ago and spread worldwide, and the fossil and DNA evidence for it.

item.title: The Human Family Tree Explained
item.description: The human family tree explained: the major hominin genera and species, how they're related, and how scientists reconstruct the tree from fossils and DNA.

item.title: Human Evolution Timeline: 7 Million Years Explained
item.description: A clear human evolution timeline from 7 million years ago to today — Sahelanthropus, Lucy, Homo erectus, Neanderthals and the rise of modern Homo sapiens.

item.title: How Do Scientists Date Fossils? Methods Explained
item.description: How do scientists date fossils? A clear guide to radiocarbon, potassium-argon, uranium-series, luminescence, and the methods behind every date on this site.

item.title: Why Did Neanderthals Go Extinct? Evidence from Fossils and DNA
item.description: Neanderthals vanished 40,000 years ago in Europe. Was it competition, climate, small populations, or interbreeding with humans? The science explained.

item.title: Did Humans Evolve From Apes? The Real Story of Our Origins
item.description: Humans didn't evolve from apes—we ARE apes and share common ancestors with chimps. Learn what science actually says about human evolution and our primate

item.title: Hominin vs Hominid: What's the Difference in Evolution
item.description: Hominin and hominid mean different things in evolutionary biology. Learn the taxonomy, why the terms changed, and which word to use.

item.title: Humans vs Chimpanzees: How Different Are We Really?
item.description: Humans and chimpanzees share 98.8% DNA but evolved in strikingly different directions. Discover what the genetic similarity really means and how we diverged.

item.title: Why Did Humans Start Walking Upright? Origins of Bipedalism
item.description: Discover why hominins evolved to walk on two legs millions of years before big brains emerged. Explore fossils, anatomy, and the surprising truths about

item.title: How Much Neanderthal DNA Do You Have? Ancestry Breakdown
item.description: Learn what percentage of Neanderthal DNA you carry. Discover how much archaic ancestry is in modern humans and what it actually does.

item.title: Denisovan DNA in Modern Humans: Who Carries It & Why
item.description: Discover Denisovan DNA in your genes. Explore where it survives, why Tibetans have altitude superpowers, and what ancient interbreeding reveals about human

item.title: Sima de los Huesos vs Denisova Cave: Ancient DNA Discoveries
item.description: Two caves transformed human evolution science. Sima de los Huesos revealed early Neanderthals; Denisova Cave discovered an entirely new human lineage through

item.title: Jebel Irhoud vs Omo Kibish: Which was modern humans' birthplace?
item.description: Jebel Irhoud and Omo Kibish hold the oldest Homo sapiens fossils. Discover how these African sites rewrote human origins to 300,000+ years ago.

item.title: Venus figurines: Ice Age art across 40,000 years
item.description: Venus figurines are small carved figures made by early humans across Ice Age Europe. Discover why they matter to understanding human creativity.

item.title: When Did Humans Control Fire? Evidence & Timeline
item.description: Discover when humans first controlled fire. Explore archaeological evidence from 1.5 million years ago to habitual hearth use.

item.title: Mitochondrial Eve vs Y-chromosomal Adam: Our Genetic Ancestors
item.description: Mitochondrial Eve vs Y-chromosomal Adam explained: who they really were, why they never met, and why they were not the first or only humans who ever lived.

item.title: Stone Knapping Methods: How Humans Learned to Shape Stone
item.description: Stone knapping methods explained: from hard-hammer percussion to Levallois cores and pressure flaking — how the craft of shaping stone tools evolved over

item.title: Ice Age Predators of North Carolina: What Paleoindians Faced
item.description: Ice Age predators in North Carolina: meet the dire wolves, saber-toothed cats, giant short-faced bears and American lions Paleoindians faced before 9000 BC.

item.title: Paranthropus vs Australopithecus: Robust vs Gracile
item.description: Paranthropus vs Australopithecus: how the heavy-jawed 'robust' australopiths differ from the lighter 'gracile' ones in skull, diet and evolutionary fate —

item.description: Lascaux vs Chauvet: compare France's two most famous painted caves — their age, animals, artistic technique and discovery — and why Chauvet rewrote the story

item.title: Homo sapiens vs Neanderthals: How Are We Different?
item.description: Homo sapiens vs Neanderthals: compare brain, skull, body and behaviour of modern humans and our closest extinct cousins — and why only one lineage survived.

item.title: Homo habilis vs Homo erectus: Dawn of Our Genus
item.description: Homo habilis vs Homo erectus: how the small 'handy man' differs from tall, far-travelling erectus in body, brain and tools — and why they were neighbours,

item.title: Homo erectus vs Homo sapiens: Body, Brain & Brawn
item.description: Homo erectus vs Homo sapiens: how the first human with a modern body compares to us in brain, skull, range and technology — and whether erectus was our

item.title: Cro-Magnon vs Neanderthal: The First Modern Europeans
item.description: Cro-Magnon vs Neanderthal: who were the Cro-Magnons, how did they differ from Neanderthals, and did they replace them?

item.title: Homo naledi's Burial Behavior: Did a Small-Brained Human Bury Its Dead?
item.description: The Homo naledi burial claim says a small-brained hominin buried its dead some 240,000 years ago. Did it really happen, or are the skeptics right to doubt it?

item.title: Archaic vs Anatomically Modern Homo sapiens: What "Modern" Means
item.description: Archaic vs anatomically modern Homo sapiens: a 315,000-year-old face, an old-shaped skull, and what the word "modern" really means for our own species.

item.title: Homo antecessor: Europe's Mysterious Pioneer — The Modern Face Puzzle
item.description: Discover Homo antecessor, Europe's earliest known human: an 800,000-year-old skull with a surprisingly modern face, the first cannibalism, and a contested past.

item.title: Homo heidelbergensis vs Neanderthals: Ancestor or Not?
item.description: Homo heidelbergensis vs Neanderthals: was heidelbergensis the direct ancestor of the Neanderthals? Compare their brains, tools, and the fossils that link them.

item.title: Australopithecus afarensis vs africanus: Lucy vs Mrs Ples
item.description: Australopithecus afarensis vs africanus: how Lucy's East African species differs from South Africa's africanus in skull, teeth, age and family-tree place.

item.title: Homo floresiensis vs Homo erectus: The Hobbit Debate
item.description: Homo floresiensis vs Homo erectus: did the metre-tall 'hobbit' shrink from tall, wide-ranging Homo erectus? Island dwarfism and the Flores fossils explained.

item.title: Homo naledi vs Australopithecus: What's the Difference?
item.description: Homo naledi vs Australopithecus: why a small-brained relative from 300,000 years ago looks two million years out of date — anatomy, dating and the debate.

item.title: Ardipithecus vs Australopithecus: What Changed at 4 Ma
item.description: Ardipithecus vs Australopithecus: how Ardi's grasping foot and woodland life differ from Lucy's bipedalism — and what it reveals about upright walking.

item.title: Neanderthals vs Denisovans: How Are They Different?
item.description: Neanderthals vs Denisovans compared: their split, fossils, tools, and the interbreeding that still lives in human DNA today. Discover what sets them apart.
